frontier.label: Arithmetic-to-zero-location rigidity
frontier.target: Prove the verified quantitative upper bound for the weighted Chebyshev logarithmic average strongly enough to dominate the exact entropy cost, then derive an unconditional zero-location constraint

goal: A complete Lean-verified proof of the Riemann hypothesis

milestones.label: Boundary heat vanishing is equivalent to RH
Poisson decay is equivalent to sublinear cumulative upper spectral height
Smooth endpoint drift is summable and work is asymptotic to the logarithmic average plus log N
Suzuki logarithmic Mellin atoms evaluate to von-Mangoldt Dirichlet terms

presentation: verified theorem inventory; milestones are not a proof chain
statusNote: Cutoffs zero and one are proved. For Suzuki's logarithmic-average error A_N, Lean proves E_endpoint(N)=-A_N-log(N)-4 and rewrites the exact entropy and sufficient quadratic conditions as upper bounds for A_N. Every unit smooth drift satisfies 0 <= D(b,b+1) <= b^(-3/2), so signed mass-error work minus A_N minus log(N) converges to an explicit finite constant. Lean now extends the literal logarithmic-average formula to every real b >= 1 and evaluates each integrable real Mellin atom exactly as its von-Mangoldt Dirichlet term; the square-root main term contributes 4/(sigma-1). The infinite sum-integral exchange, full zeta logarithmic-derivative identity, required upper bound for A_N, and every RH-forcing zero-location step remain open.
